description.narrative: Aperçu de l'ensemble des soutiens de Gavi à Somalie (la). À ce niveau, l'évaluation conjointe, le plan pluriannuel du pays, le rapport d'étape annuel sont fournis comme pièces justificatives. Pour plus de détails sur chaque soutien, veuillez-vous référer aux activités ci-dessous.

Parent Activity of Gavi's Support to Somalia At this level, Joint Appraisal, Country Multi Year Plan, Annual Progress Report are provided as supporting documents. In 2020/2021, as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, Multi-stakeholder dialogue (MSD) documents temporarily replaced the traditional Joint Appraisal to ensure that Gavi’s continuing support to the EPI programme be aligned with realities at country level. For details on each vaccine please refer to child activities.

Note technique: Toutes les activités des pays soutenus par Gavi ont un statut «mise en œuvre» et par conséquent, aucune date de fin réelle est déterminée. Les pays éligibles peuvent soumettre des propositions et demandes de soutien à Gavi à tout moment.
Technical note: all Gavi Country activities have a status of "Implementation" and no Actual End Date, as qualifying countries are able to submit proposals to Gavi at any stage.

description.narrative: The comprehensive multi-year plan (cMYP) is a single plan which consolidates several immunisation activities. It is a key planning and management tool for national immunisation programmes. It addresses global, national, and subnational immunisation objectives and strategies, and evaluates the costs and financing of the programme in line with the WHO-UNICEF Global Immunization Vision and Strategy 2006-2015. Gavi requires countries to submit a cMYP along with the standard proposal form when applying for Gavi support (ISS, INS, and NVS). In 2006, over 50 countries had developed cMYPs using the WHO-UNICEF cMYP guidelines and costing tool. The cMYP replaces the financial sustainability plan (FSP), used to assess the funding challenges of a country's national immunisation programme within the broader health financing context and to describe the government’s approach to mobilising and effectively using resources to support medium- and long-term immunisation objectives.

description.narrative: L’évaluation conjointe est une évaluation nationale, multi-parties prenantes de l’avancement de la mise en œuvre et de la performance des subventions allouées au titre du soutien aux vaccins et en espèces, et de sa contribution à l’amélioration des services de vaccination. Il en résulte un « rapport de l’évaluation conjointe », qui fait état de la performance de la subvention Gavi, ainsi que des défis liés à la mise en œuvre. Le rapport de l’évaluation conjointe guide les discussions menées avec l’instance de coordination nationale concernée sur les domaines où des investissements et des efforts accrus, ainsi qu’un soutien technique, sont requis.

The joint appraisal is an in-country, multi-stakeholder review of the implementation progress and performance of Gavi's vaccine and cash grant support to the country, and of its contribution to improved immunisation outcomes. The outcome of the appraisal is the completed "joint appraisal report" that captures Gavi grant performance as well as implementation challenges. The joint appraisal report informs discussions with national coordination mechanisms on areas where greater national investments and efforts, as well as technical support, are needed.

condition.narrative: Funds must be used for the agreed immunisation activities (inactivated polio, measles, oral cholera, pentavalent, pneumococcal and rotavirus vaccines, among others; health-system strengthening and cold-chain support; COVID-19 vaccine support), meeting the programmatic, coverage and equity targets and the monitoring and reporting requirements set out in the country's decision letters and partnership agreements, the joint appraisal and annual progress reporting.

Gavi support to Somalia is conditional on alignment with the national immunisation strategy and comprehensive multi-year plan, and on compliance with Gavi's eligibility, transition and sustainability policies. The applicable policy conditions are set out in the country's decision letters and partnership agreements.

Somalia must meet its vaccine co-financing obligations and comply with financial management, funds-flow, audit and data-quality requirements. The specific co-financing amounts and fiduciary terms are set out in the Gavi co-financing policy and the country's decision letters and partnership agreements.
